clue.text: It's likely 6 ac is up, having been disturbed

indicators.note: letters that have been disturbed are knocked out of order, so the pool is reshuffled

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 6 across, the name of Miss Wilfer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reckons the girl at 6 across has probably woken up after being disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been disturbed' shuffles BELLA (from 6 across) with IS UP; 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plausible story is a believable or probable one, so it is a synonym for likely.

clue.text: One out of David's book for him, say

definitions.meaning: one of the songs traditionally ascribed to King David in the Bible
the word him sounds like hymn, a sacred song

explanation.definitionFit: One of the Old Testament's sacred songs credited to David is also a hymn, which him sounds like.

clue.text: Sake can set one squinting

indicators.note: set means arranged in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rice wine can leave someone cross-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges the letters of SAKE and CAN; 'one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look sideways or obliquely, as if squinting.

clue.text: Not a period for the half-French settler

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half
colon is French for a colonist or settler

explanation.surface: It was a temporary posting for the part-French colonist.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark makes a pause but is not a full stop.

clue.text: Peripatetic seaside hairdresser?

parts.note: read literally, someone combing the shore, roaming the coast picking up flotsam

explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer who searches the shore for flotsam is pictured as someone who grooms the beach.

clue.text: Stop a boundary

definitions.meaning: to finish or halt
a limit or extremity

explanation.definitionFit: To finish something and the limit of something share the one word.

clue.text: Miss Wilfer, the beautiful Italian

definitions.meaning: ... Wilfer is the heroine of Dickens's novel Our Mutual Friend
the Italian word for beautiful, in its feminine form

explanation.definitionFit: Bella is the first name of Dickens's Miss Wilfer and also Italian for a pretty woman or thing.

clue.text: It sounds a lot of money for a sweet

indicators.note: the clue says the dessert is pronounced like the word for a fortune

parts.note: a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in cost a bomb

explanation.surface: A dessert sounds as though it costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cost a bomb' is British slang for very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert.

clue.text: Messenger taking English — he is gifted

indicators.note: taking means the abbreviation is added on after the envoy

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or emissary

explanation.surface: An envoy takes up English and proves talented.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is someone left property in a will, so a person who is given a bequest.

clue.text: Prepared to strike, having made a speech

definitions.meaning: a golfer addresses the ball, lining up to hit it
spoken formally to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer lines up on the ball before hitting, and a speaker talks to a crowd: both use this verb.

clue.text: Morning sounds

parts.note: the old military signallers' spoken alphabet said the letters of the morning abbreviation as two code words

explanation.definitionFit: In First World War signalese the letters A and M were spoken as two code words, so the phrase means before noon.

clue.text: Mother became old and spoilt

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: A mother grew old and became indulged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged has been harmed or ruined, which is what spoilt means here.

clue.text: The chap superintending is out of his mind

parts.note: a chap is a man
IC is short for in charge, which is what superintending means

explanation.surface: The man in charge has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: IC stands for 'in charge', a common abbreviation; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manic person is frenzied or crazed, so near to being mad.

clue.text: Radio and TV flashes: "Women for Peace"

parts.note: radio and television are the broadcast media
trices are instants, as in in a trice

explanation.surface: Broadcast news bulletins announce a women's peace movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediatrices is the plural of mediatrix, a female mediator who brings parties to peace.

clue.text: A bow to match

definitions.meaning: a bow ... in a ribbon or cravat
to draw level with, as in a game that ends level

explanation.definitionFit: A knot such as a bow-tie is one kind, and drawing level in a contest is the other sense.

clue.text: Straight hit in international cricket — go for a run

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a drive is a straight batting stroke in cricket

explanation.surface: A straight shot in a Test match lets the batsman take a run.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match and a drive a forward batting stroke; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To try out a car on the road before buying it is to take it for a spin.

clue.text: Inspect obelisks in glare

parts.note: to look at something is to inspect it
an obelisk or obelus is the printer's dagger symbol

explanation.surface: Someone examines tall stone monuments in bright sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing an obelisk is the dagger mark used for footnotes; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To look daggers is an idiom for staring angrily at someone.

clue.text: Fool is to play this

parts.note: the British idiom for fooling around names a skittish farm animal

explanation.definitionFit: To act the fool is an idiom about larking like a frisky animal.

clue.text: It assists the diver to go up rather than down

definitions.text: It assists the diver to go up rather than down

parts.words: It assists the diver to go up rather than down
parts.note: a diver at a swimming pool bounces upward off a flexible plank before falling into the water

explanation.definitionFit: A pool's flexible diving plank launches divers upward before their plunge.

clue.text: Let go of a catch

definitions.meaning: to free or set loose
a lever or catch that frees a mechanism

explanation.definitionFit: Freeing something and the device that frees a mechanism are both called by this word.

clue.text: Half an Indian town is turning into wet earth

indicators.note: turning means the kept half is read backwards
only the first half of the town's doubled name is kept for the answer

parts.note: Dum Dum is a town near Kolkata, which gave its name to the dumdum bullet

explanation.surface: Part of an Indian town is turning into a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' leaves DUM, and 'is turning' turns it round; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud is soft, wet soil.

clue.text: Camphor used in garment holder

indicators.note: the answer is used inside the two words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Mothballs are used in a wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Menthol is also called peppermint camphor, a waxy compound from mint oil.

clue.text: In retreat, ran down the King's rescuer

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word for ran down is read in reverse

parts.note: to run down someone is to revile or criticise them
ER is a royal cipher, here Edward Rex, the King

explanation.surface: Fleeing, someone criticised the man who saved the King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' turns REVILED into DELIVER; ER is a royal monogram, here read as Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets a person free from danger is a saviour or liberator.

clue.text: Looks for spectacles

definitions.meaning: glances or sights
sights or scenes, not glasses

explanation.definitionFit: Glances and scenes both go by this word.

clue.text: American city without a ruler for ages

indicators.note: without means the ruler's letters are removed from the city

parts.note: Yonkers is a city in New York State
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: A US city has had no leader for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang meaning a very long time.

clue.text: Having edges supported

definitions.meaning: with faces or flanks
took the part of

explanation.definitionFit: A shape with faces and someone who backed another share the word.

clue.text: Picture on the line is ornate illustration

parts.note: an image is a picture
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A picture of a railway track is an elaborate drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is a standard abbreviation for railway; 'on' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is vivid descriptive or figurative language, a richly decorated picture in words.

clue.text: One tree's sound

indicators.note: sound means the tree's name is said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: a yew is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A single tree makes a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: One and you both serve as an impersonal pronoun meaning people in general.

clue.text: Suited the bumpkin to go outside

indicators.note: the word for bumpkin is to go round the outside of the word 'the'

parts.note: a clod is a lout or yokel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suit fitted the country yokel when he went out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be suited is to be dressed, wearing garments.

clue.text: Makes uniform for squares

definitions.meaning: to make level or regular
settles up so that both sides are level

explanation.definitionFit: To level something and to square accounts both mean making things equal.

clue.text: Insecure has not been paid

definitions.meaning: shaky or unstable
describing a bill or debt still outstanding

explanation.definitionFit: An unstable situation and an outstanding bill are both described by the same word.
